lines.text: Spring in Harrow's Rest. The green is mud, and the table in the middle of it is three planks long.
You have a satchel, two heels of bread, a little coin, and one day.
Walk the green. Look at people properly. [E] near someone to notice them.
Marta sits on the bakery step with her hands in her lap. The oven behind her is cold.
There's flour on her apron, but it's old flour.
Already ate.
He says it before you ask. His lunch tin is empty. It was empty yesterday too.
Tobias is at the anvil. Six good hoes hang on his wall, and half the village is turning soil with sticks.
He doesn't look up. He knows you're there.
You've already taken them in this morning.
Midday. You have the afternoon's attention to spend. [E] near someone to see what you could do.
The afternoon is spent. The light is going gold. [N] to head to the table.
You can sit again, if you like. I'm not much company.
Your loaves will be ready by dusk.
Oh. The newcomer. Mind the mud.
Somebody left bread on the step. Wasn't you, was it? ...Good bread, anyway.
I said I was fine.
I'm not hungry, if that's what you're asking.
Scrap's sorted. Didn't ask you to.
He doesn't say thank you. He doesn't tell you to leave, either.
You again.
Hoe working? Don't bring it back bent.
If you're here to borrow something, the answer's no.
You leave a heel of bread on the step, wrapped in a cloth, and walk on without looking back.
When you pass again, the cloth is folded neatly. The bread is gone.
Pip! Here. You look half starved.
Heads turn. Pip takes the bread, because everyone is watching. His ears go red.
...Thanks.
There's a frog by the river as big as a loaf. I named him Elder Caldwell. Don't tell.
He talks about frogs for a long time. You let him.
You sit beside Marta on the step. Neither of you says much for a while.
Henrik used to sing while the dough rose. Terrible voice. Truly terrible.
She laughs, then stops, then decides she doesn't mind that she laughed.
You clear years of soot from the flue. It draws clean now.
That's kind of you. It still needs someone to light it.
I'll pay you to bake for tonight.
...All right. Coin's coin.
She counts it twice and doesn't meet your eye.
I don't need help. I need people to stop offering it.
He turns back to the anvil. The conversation is over.
You come back anyway. You don't ask. You start sorting his scrap pile by length.
The hammering stops for a moment.
...Long pieces on the left.
Two coin. Don't bring it back bent.
You have a good hoe now.
Dusk. Lanterns come out one at a time. People drift toward the table, or they don't.
Marta sits beside you and passes the salt before you ask for it.
Marta takes the end of the bench. She's polite. She'll leave early.
Marta's window is dark. She doesn't come.
Pip squeezes onto the bench and eats slowly, like he's making it last.
Nobody comments. That's the kindness.
Pip hovers by the fence, then sits at the far end with his hands in his pockets.
Pip doesn't come. Someone says he went home early.
Tobias sets down a bench nobody asked him to mend.
Table was wobbling.
Tobias stands at the edge with his arms crossed. But he stays.
The forge is still ringing. Tobias doesn't come.
The talk goes quiet. You could say something about your day.
Busy day! Fed Pip, helped Marta out, sorted things with Tobias...
People nod. Someone says, "That's good of you." The table gets a little quieter.
You eat. You listen. Somebody tells a story about the flood year, and for once it ends with a joke.
Marta finds a reason to go home.
When you look for Pip, his place is empty.
Tobias grunts and walks back to the forge.
Morning. There is smoke coming from the bakery chimney.
Couldn't sleep. Thought I'd see if my hands still knew how.
She's kneading. She's humming. It's a terrible voice. It's wonderful.
Morning. The oven is lit. A neat row of loaves waits by the door.
Anything else?
The door closes. Not hard. Just closed.
Morning. The bakery is quiet. The oven is still cold.
Marta is on the step again, hands in her lap.
